transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… mostly it’s work stuff. I’m a sales supervisor, and I keep making these stupid mistakes on reports—like copying the wrong numbers off the team dashboard, or I’ll miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check even though I swear I looked it over. It’s embarrassing, because I’m not trying to be careless.

And then I start second-guessing myself, going back through things, which reminds me of this one time our dashboard layout changed and everyone was messing it up—but mine keeps happening even when nothing changed. So… yeah, that’s kind of what pushed me to come in.
Thinking back, did you notice similar problems with attention, carelessness, or forgetfulness when you were in school or as a child, or is this something that started more recently in adulthood?

Yeah, no, it definitely goes way back. My mom still brings it up sometimes—like she’ll joke about these teacher notes from elementary school saying I rushed through my work or lost homework.

And, uh… I remember getting in trouble for talking when I wasn’t supposed to. Or not even trouble exactly, just always being told, like, “Wait your turn,” “sit down,” that kind of thing. Which is funny because my mom saved everything—report cards, little art projects, even this terrible clay bowl I made in like third grade—but the notes were always the same kind of thing. So yeah, it wasn’t just something that started with work.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or find yourself interrupting others or having trouble staying seated in situations where you're expected to, even now as an adult?

Yeah, definitely the restless part. Like if I’m in a long meeting, it’s almost like my body is buzzing on the inside. I’ll be shifting around in the chair, tapping my foot, messing with a pen, that kind of thing.

Sometimes I’ll make up a reason to get up, like grabbing water or checking something, even if I don’t really need to. Long meetings are the worst for that.
Aside from these work situations, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like health, finances, or relationships—and having a hard time controlling that worry?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I worry about stuff like anybody, I guess, but I don’t know that it’s, like, a bunch of different things all the time.

Work will get in my head, sure, and then I’ll start thinking about something totally unrelated, like whether I paid the electric bill, and then I remember this one time I set the autopay wrong and got a late fee—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I’m not sure I’d call it excessive worry. It’s more like my mind jumps around, if that makes sense.
Do you notice these same problems with distractibility, restlessness, or forgetfulness affecting you outside of work too—like at home, in relationships, or during errands and chores?

Yeah, it’s not just work. It’s at home too, for sure.

Like I’ll forget regular life stuff—returning calls I’m supposed to make, even important ones, like from my attorney, and then I’ll see the voicemail later and feel like an idiot. Or a bill will sit there until I get the late notice, even though I meant to pay it. I’ll tell my kids, “Yeah, I’ll bring that home,” like something they needed, and then I walk in empty-handed because I got distracted by something else.

And then I try to write stuff down, but sometimes I forget where I wrote it down, which is… yeah. It’s frustrating.
Do you often find yourself interrupting people mid-conversation, finishing their sentences, or blurting out responses before they've finished speaking?

Yeah… I do that, especially in meetings. Somebody will be explaining something and I’ll think I already know where they’re going, so I jump in with the answer or start responding before they’re done.

And then half the time I realize, like, wait, that wasn’t even the point they were making, or I cut them off and now it’s awkward. I try not to, but it kind of comes out before I’ve fully thought it through.

Have you ever gone through distinct periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elated, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your thoughts were racing more than usual, separate from your everyday restlessness?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like several days where I’m, like, on top of the world or barely sleeping and totally fine.

I mean, my mind races sometimes, but that feels more like the usual jumping-around thing, not some separate stretch of time. And sleep… I might stay up too late because I get caught on something, like a video or looking up one thing that turns into twenty things, but then I’m tired the next day. So I don’t think it’s that kind of thing you’re asking about.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out bipolar disorder (no distinct episodes of elevated mood, decreased sleep, or racing thoughts) and generalized anxiety disorder (worry not excessive or pervasive across domains). Symptoms remain consistent with combined inattentive-hyperactive-impulsive ADHD, present since childhood and across multiple settings.
